column2: [LSP Connect] - My manager - email: sittharl@scg.com can not connect to WiFi
column12: P3  (This represent an issue impact to area or group and have working around)
column31:
Resolution (Point‑to‑Point – Easy to Understand)
1. Issue Summary
User Sittharl was unable to connect to LSPConnect Wi‑Fi.
Cisco ISE logs showed that authentication was successful, but authorization was denied.
Endpoint MAC address: 14:75:5B:A7:31:09

2. Root Cause
The endpoint did not match any authorization rule that allows network access.
The 802.1X session fell back to the Default Authorization Rule.
The default rule applied the Authorization Profile: DenyAccess.
As a result, Cisco ISE returned a RADIUS Access‑Reject.
This issue was not related to the password or Active Directory authentication.
3. Action Taken by LV2: added the endpoint MAC address to the whitelist in Cisco ISE.MAC Address: 14:75:5B:A7:31:09
4. Result
The endpoint successfully reconnected to LSPConnect Wi‑Fi.
No further Access‑Reject events were observed.
The user is now able to access the network normally.

This issue was resolved by deleting the folder:OneDrive\Apps\Microsoft Edge\Edge Workspaces 
Removing this folder cleared the corrupted Workspace data stored in OneDrive, which had been blocking synchronization.
The root cause is likely an account sync problem where Edge Workspaces data stored in OneDrive becomes corrupted or stuck, especially after account migrations or when multiple accounts are used. When the Workspace data inside:
OneDrive\Apps\Microsoft Edge\Edge Workspaces
is corrupted, Microsoft Edge cannot sync properly through OneDrive, resulting in Workspaces failing to load.
The Workspaces feature in Microsoft Edge does not work with my account - Microsoft Q&A

Additionally, Microsoft has acknowledged that the current sync issues with Edge Workspaces stored in OneDrive are due to the outdated Workspace architecture.
Microsoft is now migrating Workspaces off OneDrive/SharePoint and moving them to a dedicated Edge Sync service to prevent such issues.
Workspaces in Edge: Upcoming migration to improved architecture - M365 Admin

column31:
1) Issue:LSPConnect
Windows showed a warning: “LSPConnect isn’t secure / older security standard” and Event Viewer errors (12013 / 8002 / 8004 – Explicit EAP failure).
ISE showed (when the issue occurred) reported Authentication succeeded (5200) but included: 
Connect‑Info = "CONNECT 0Mbps 802.11b", indicating the radio link fell back to legacy 802.11b with no effective data throughput, even though EAP authentication passed.


2) Actions before the issue was solved:
Forget the LSPConnect network in Windows.
Turn Wi‑Fi off (radio off) for ~30 seconds (Airplane Mode is fine), then turn it back on.
Reconnect to LSPConnect and re‑enter AD credentials.
Outcome: Connection became stable and secure. The Windows warning disappeared; the new ISE session showed a healthy 802.1X/EAP session with normal data-plane parameters.

3) Why this works =>“Forget + Wi‑Fi off/on” does three important resets:
Clears the 802.1X profile (PEAP settings, certificate pinning, PMK cache, saved credentials), eliminating any corrupt or incompatible parameters.
Resets the supplicant and radio state (tears down pairwise keys, rate sets, and any partial handshakes).
Forces a full re‑negotiation: fresh PEAP/TLS handshake, new 4‑way handshake, proper data rates/ciphers—bringing the session back to the compliant WPA2‑Enterprise baseline.
